mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend over the past 6 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% for three consecutive months indicates a weak labor market, which suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production growth below 1.0% year-over-year during high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals supply chain constraints that increase corporate costs and reduce profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: supply chain constraints during high inflation
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts over the past 6 months indicates strengthening consumer demand for residential construction, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST has increased for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth and rising unemployment rate indicate a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both PAYEMS growth declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%) and rising federal funds rate, the market anticipates a shift to tighter monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS increase > 0.1% in last month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
